phase1.intro:
Everything we've saved to disk so far has been text or bytes we manually built by hand. Serialization does something genuinely different.

Where do you want to start?

topics.buttonText: What does implementing Serializable actually require?
dialogue: It takes a whole object, exactly as it exists in memory, packs it into a form written to a file, and later unpacks it back into a real, working object. The only requirement is implementing [[term:Serializable]] — a genuinely unusual interface with zero methods.
[[key:It's a marker interface — its whole job is just telling Java "objects of this class are allowed to be packed up like this"]], nothing more.

stickyNote.flavor: 🏷️ a sticker that says "shippable", no methods needed
stickyNote.definition: Serializable has zero methods to implement — it's a marker interface that just tells Java a class's objects can be serialized.

topics.buttonText: How do ObjectOutputStream and ObjectInputStream work?
dialogue: [[term:ObjectOutputStream]].writeObject(obj) does the actual packing, and [[term:ObjectInputStream]].readObject() unpacks it again — though readObject() hands you back a plain Object, so [[key:you always need to cast it back to the real type]], like `(Person) ois.readObject()`.

stickyNote.flavor: 📦 pack with writeObject, cast back after readObject
stickyNote.definition: writeObject(obj) serializes an object; readObject() deserializes it but returns Object, requiring an explicit cast back to the real type.

topics.buttonText: What gets left out of serialization, and what's serialVersionUID?
dialogue: [[term:transient]] fields are deliberately EXCLUDED from serialization — good for something like a password. [[warn:static fields are never serialized either]] — they belong to the CLASS, not any object.
[[key:serialVersionUID is a version marker you should always define explicitly]] — without it, Java auto-generates one, and if the class structure changes, old files can fail to unpack.

stickyNote.flavor: 🚫 excluded fields, and a version marker worth setting
stickyNote.definition: transient fields are excluded from serialization; static fields never serialize. serialVersionUID should be defined explicitly to avoid version mismatches.

phase1.openingDialogue: Serialization packs a whole object's in-memory state to disk and unpacks it later — marked with Serializable, versioned with serialVersionUID. 📦

phase2.errorMessage:
Exception in thread "main" java.io.NotSerializableException: Person
        at java.base/java.io.ObjectOutputStream.writeObject0(ObjectOutputStream.java:1185)
        at java.base/java.io.ObjectOutputStream.writeObject(ObjectOutputStream.java:349)
        at Test.main(Test.java:16)
phase2.explanation:
Person never implements Serializable, so the moment oos.writeObject(p) tries to actually serialize it, Java discovers there's no permission slip on file for this class and throws NotSerializableException at runtime.

[[warn:this is checked at runtime, not compile time]] — the code compiles just fine; the failure only shows up the instant you actually try to serialize an object of a class that isn't marked Serializable.

[[key:the fix is exactly what the marker interface exists for]]: class Person implements Serializable { ... }. And it's worth knowing this rule extends deeper than just the top-level object — every field's type inside Person also needs to be Serializable (or marked transient), because serialization has to be able to save the ENTIRE object graph, not just the outermost layer.
phase2.openingDialogue: Watch what happens when an "exception" — wait, when a class forgets to sign up for serialization~

phase3.openingDialogue: Let's save an object to disk and bring it back~

mcq.question:
Which field is correctly excluded from an object's serialized form?

A) A regular private instance field
B) A field marked transient
C) A field with a public getter
D) The first field declared in the class

phase4.selfChallenge:
Create a Student class that:
• Implements Serializable
• Has fields: name, id, gpa
• Has a transient field: password
• Has serialVersionUID = 1L

In main:
1. Create a Student object
2. Serialize it to "student.ser"
3. Deserialize it back
4. Print both the original and restored objects

Note: The transient field should be null after deserialization.

phase5.trivia: [[fun:Fun fact]]: Java's ObjectOutputStream format is notoriously version-fragile and has been a recurring source of real security vulnerabilities — deserializing untrusted data (readObject() on a file or stream you don't fully control) has been exploited in several major real-world attacks, which is part of why many modern Java codebases avoid built-in serialization in favor of formats like JSON for anything crossing a trust boundary.
phase5.openingDialogue: One more thought before you go~
